newsitem.title: SPAIN: Summary of Spanish regional debt, 1997 issue plans. [CORRECTED 10:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Summary of Spanish regional debt, 1997 issue plans. [CORRECTED 10:42 GMT]

text.p: Spanish regional debt is set to increase next year, with many of the 17 regions expected to go to market with new issues, according to a Reuters survey.
Although it is too early to present a detailed plan for every region, the following offers a brief desciption of the regions' expected 1997 net debt and plans to fund it.

The summary, formed from calls made by Reuters to various regions, excludes four regions of the five that have yet to issue any bonds. Cantabria, which is expected to make its debut in 1997, has been included in the survey.
***ANDALUCIA***
Andalucia, together with Valencia and Catalonia, holds regular public auctions, organized under the same system used by the Spanish Treasury.

Andalucia has bi-monthly auctions on bills of maturities between three- and 18-months and one monthly auction of three-, five- and 10-year bonds. Currently, Andalucia has a programme to issue up to 160 bln pesetas (pta) in bonds. Of this programme, it has already issued 147.6 bln pta this year. It expects to add 90 bln pta to this programme in coming months.

Under law, Andalucia may increase its net new debt up to 63 bln pta in 1996 and up to 33.40 bln pta in 1997. Apart from periodic auctions, Andalucia is also considering the possibility of launching a foreign bond or one Eurobond next year.
***BALEARES***
The Balearic islands has outstanding a 15-bln pta bond issued at the end of June 1996. They are planning no further issues in 1997.
***CANARIAS***

The Canary Islands had bonds of 35 bln pta outstanding as of June 1995. It is issuing bonds tailored for the region's firms, with a low coupon and fiscal advantages for local companies. The region's net new debt has a limit at eight bln pta in 1996. It is expected that this cap will be reduced to 4.7 bln in 1997.
***CANTABRIA***

Cantabria, Spain's second smallest region, has yet to tap the capital market. But in 1997, it plans to hit the domestic market with four bln pta bonds with a maturity of five-years or more. The issue could be made in April or May. It may follow up with more issuance if market conditions permit.
***CASTILLA-LA MANCHA***

The net new debt had a ceiling at 7.13 billion pesetas in 1996, which was completely used this year with bank loans in the domestic market. This cap has been reduced to 3.4 billion pta for 1997. It intends to launch bonds and banks loans both domestic in pesetas and foreign in many currencies.
***CASTILLA Y LEON***
In 1997, it has a ceiling of 12.7 bln pta for net new debt. It wants to issue a maximum of 10 bln pta in bonds, but the exact amount and method will depend on market conditions.
***CATALONIA***
Last month, the region launched a new programme of public auctions, similar to those already in use in Andalucia and Valencia.
Catalonia plans to issue around 10 bln pta bonds in five- and ten-year bonds each month, up to a total of 30 bln pesetas this year and 120 bln pta in 1997.

Authorization to issue 50 bln in the domestic market is still pending, but it hasn't yet issued the up to 20 bln pta in the foreign market for which it already has permission. It said it might add this to next year's programme, bringing 1997 foreign market issuance up to a total 40/50 billion pesetas.
***GALICIA***

Galicia was active and quite innovative in 1996, issuing net new debt of 35 billion pesetas plus new issues to replace debt that matured. In 1996, it launched a 14 bln pta five-year bond in the domestic market and 16 bln in the 10-year segment.
They also launched a Caravela bond for 10 billion escudos with a maturity of seven years. The European Investment Bank (EIB) arranged a syndicated loan of 10.8 bln pta for the region.
In 1997, the region's net new debt can rise up to 24 bln pta.
***MADRID***

The region will end 1996 with net new debt of 19.68 bln pta, bringing the total outstanding to 368.33 bln pta. In 1996, gross issues were launched for 54.52 bln pta including an EIB syndicated loan for 10 bln pta, new bonds for 15 bln pta, indexed bonds for 10 bln pta, domestic syndicated loans for 16 bln pta and 3.52 bln (bilateral operations). Next year's net new debt can rise up to 10 bln pta.
***MURCIA***
For the coming year, net new debt can rise 12 billion pesetas. Typically, it relies more on bank loans than on new bond issuance. It has yet to decide on how to fund it.
***NAVARRE***

With a total amount of bonds maturing in 1997 of 15 billion pesetas, plus a new debt limit of 8 billion pestas, the Navarre region could issue in 1997 up to a maximum of 23 bln pta. But it said it has no intention of issuing more than 15 bln.
The funding programme on the market will be tied to tax receipts, it said. Usually, it offers bonds to institutional investors, leaving only ten percent to retail investors.
***BASQUE COUNTRY***

Before the end of 1996, it is planning to issue 21 billion ptas in five-year bonds, aimed at retail investors. Earlier this month, it issued 18 bln pta in 10-yr bonds for institutional investors. The likely gross (corrects from net) debt issuance in 1997 is around 40 bln pta, but it is still not clear whether it will use domestic or foreign issuances.
***VALENCIA***

Valencia is one of the most active regions in financing matters. Its bonds are amongst the most liquid as the region holds regular auctions of bills, notes and bonds. Net new debt for 1996 was 30.73 bln pta, which has yet to be completed. It is not ruling out the possibility of issuing a new foreign bond. In 1997, net new debt rises to 37.53 bln pta. Valencia is planning to continue its regular auctions but plans to issue up to 25 percent of this amount in foreign bonds.
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
